page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 48 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processors running at 2.0 GHz, with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 960.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, delivering a combined 320 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing and memory capabilities. The server achieved a Passmark CPU score of 85426.66 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 96293.69, both placing in the top tiers. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 7649.82 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the CPU's advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX, contribute to a Passmark extended instructions score of 117918.35. LLM inference benchmarks using a small 135M model demonstrate prompt processing speeds of 10308.98 tokens per second and text generation at 377.14 tokens per second.

Given its massive memory footprint and quad-H100 GPU configuration, this server represents a high-density hardware profile. The qualitative cost efficiency is centered on high-throughput parallel processing and massive resource density, though the shared CPU allocation model and lack of bundled local storage are notable architectural tradeoffs that require external storage provisioning.

This server is optimized for large-scale artificial intelligence and machine learning workloads, including LLM training, high-throughput inference, and deep learning. The combination of 960 GB of RAM and 320 GB of GPU VRAM also makes it highly suitable for data science pipelines, complex physical simulations, and parallelized cryptographic operations.
